notes: Cosmological bounds on thermally-produced axion-like particles from Planck 2018 CMB and BAO data. Primary results are in Figs. 7 and 8. For axion-photon coupling (Fig. 7), bounds range from ~2.84×10^-8 GeV^-1 (Planck alone) to ~3.16×10^-8 GeV^-1 (Planck+BAO) for the full mass range. Data points extracted from Fig. 7 (blue diamonds, Planck+BAO case) showing approximate coupling values at each fixed axion mass. The paper also constrains axion-gluon coupling Cg/fa < 1.06×10^-7 GeV^-1 (Planck+BAO, 95% CL) and equivalent EDM coupling gd < 3.77×10^-10 GeV^-2. These are the most stringent bounds on axion-gluon coupling in the mass range 10^-4 ≲ m_a/eV ≲ 100, superseding SN1987A constraints. The bounds are mass-dependent and derived from constraints on ΔN_eff (effective number of relativistic species) via thermal production mechanisms in the early universe. | selector: text (sole candidate)
